blogs.title: Byte Latent Transformers – Reimagining Language Models Without Tokens
blogs.description: Explore how the new Byte Latent Transformer (BLT) bypasses traditional tokenization entirely, processing raw bytes directly while still achieving performance comparable to state‑of‑the‑art models like Llama 3.

blogs.title: 'Entropy Patching': Letting Data Decide Compute Allocation
blogs.description: Demystify BLT’s dynamic patching mechanism that uses next‑byte entropy predictions to decide where to group bytes into patches—shifting computational effort right where it’s needed instead of treating every token equally.

blogs.title: Inside the BLT Architecture – From Bytes to Patches and Back Again
blogs.description: Break down the three‑part design of BLT (local encoder, global latent transformer, local decoder), explaining how they collaborate through cross‑attention and hashed n‑gram embeddings to convert raw bytes into efficient contextual embeddings.

blogs.title: "Scaling That Matters": BLT Meets Llama 3 While Slashing Inference Flops
blogs.description: Review BLT’s scaling experiments that show it matches or outperforms token‑based models at similar flop budgets while achieving up to 50 % fewer inference flops through larger dynamic patches.

blogs.title: "More Than Tokens": Why Bytes Make BlT Robust to Noise and Low‑Resource Languages
blogs.description: "From noisy prompts to grapheme–phoneme conversion", see how working at the byte level gives BLT an edge in character‑level understanding, phonology tasks, and translating far‑reaching low‑resource languages.
